rules.statement: Put each capability's implementation (services, endpoints, handlers) in its own leaf package and keep it out of the composition-root package; the composition root should only reference and wire capability packages.
rules.why: When a capability is inlined in the composition root, nobody can reference it without pulling in the whole root, and its backend ends up hard-wired.
rules.check: Look for new feature code (endpoint handlers, options, capability services) added under a composition-root/server project rather than in a dedicated capability package, or capability packages that reference the composition root.

rules.statement: When a reusable capability needs a pluggable backend (such as credential verification), make it depend only on a seam interface defined in its `.Abstractions` package, never on the concrete store, persistence or crypto types.
rules.why: Inverting the dependency keeps the surface independent of any one backend, so an alternative (LDAP, external IdP, passwordless) can be plugged in without forking the surface.
rules.check: Look at a capability's handlers or services that inject concrete store or repository types, persistence, JOSE or secure-buffer types, or that build backend-specific results directly, instead of calling a seam interface from `.Abstractions`.

rules.statement: Put the concrete backend implementation of a capability seam in the package that already owns that backend's coupling, register it through that package's own opt-in extension method, and have the capability's base registration wire no default implementation.
rules.why: This keeps the backend-agnostic surface free of backend dependencies, makes each backend one opt-in among several, and follows the pattern already used for the password grant.
rules.check: Look for a base `Add…()` registration that registers a concrete backend implementation of the seam, or a backend implementation added inside the backend-agnostic capability package.

rules.statement: Define a capability's registration extension methods on the marker builder of the library it depends on (for example `IServiceBuilder<TLibrary>`), not on a plain `IServiceCollection`, so the capability cannot be added unless that library is present.
rules.why: Following the marker pattern means the compiler enforces that prerequisite libraries are registered.
rules.check: Look for new `Add…()` capability registration methods that extend `IServiceCollection` or an unrelated builder instead of the prerequisite library's marker builder.
